I recently graduated with distinction from the University of Calgary, earning a Bachelor of Science with a major in Archaeology. I currently work as an Anthropology and Archaeology Research Assistant at the University of Calgary.

My research assistant work has involved developing structured datasets from ethnographic literature, creating interactive visualizations in R, producing archaeological and ethnographic maps in QGIS, and illustrating archaeological features in Adobe Illustrator. This portfolio presents selected examples of that work.

## Selected Work

### Ethnographic Fire-Use Dataset

A structured dataset developed from ethnographic literature documenting Indigenous fire practices in northern Alberta, with information organized for comparative analysis and ecological modeling.

[View the dataset project](dataset.qmd)

### Interactive Data Visualizations

Interactive figures developed in R to explore and communicate patterns within the fire-use dataset, including its classification structure, evidence relationships, spatial forms, and timing.

[View the interactive visualizations](visualizations.qmd)

### GIS Mapping

Regional and close-up maps created in QGIS to communicate geographic context, alongside site-scale archaeological feature maps digitized from UAV orthomosaic imagery.

[View the mapping work](maps.qmd)

### Archaeological Illustration

Vector illustrations of archaeological structures and features at Kitsissut, Greenland, created in Adobe Illustrator using UAV orthomosaic imagery as reference material.

[View the illustrations](illustrations.qmd)
